grammar.title: Expressing Pain: 'Mi fa male' and 'Ho mal di'
grammar.explanation: Italian has two common constructions to express pain: 'mi fa male + body part' (literally 'it hurts me') where the body part is the subject: 'mi fa male la testa' (my head hurts), 'mi fanno male le gambe' (my legs hurt). The other construction is 'ho mal di + body part': 'ho mal di testa' (I have a headache), 'ho mal di stomaco' (I have a stomachache). Note that 'mal di' is used without the article. For more formal/medical contexts: 'sento un dolore a/al...' (I feel a pain in...).
